> **What you can defend when you leave.** Produce one honest result you can reproduce from a clean start, with its uncertainty attached.

## The milestone ahead {#checkpoint}

This is where your project produces its first real number. The milestone asks for less than you might expect: one honest result, with its uncertainty attached, reproducible from a clean start. The point is not volume. It is a result you can trace from claim to output to data cell, because every number you will ever defend in this project passes through the discipline you set here.

This studio closes with **[Milestone 7: Your first reproducible analysis](milestone07-first-analysis.qmd)**, a short chapter of its own after the lessons. **What it asks you to produce.** A route-specific result with an uncertainty statement, a restart-and-run-all verification, an environment record, and a claim-to-output check.

Milestone 8 exists to attack this result; the cleaner your record here, the more the attack can teach you. The milestone chapter keeps the working details: the practice steps, the versioned record, and how the artifact is assessed.

## The lessons in this studio

Read them in order, working each lesson's **It is your turn** as you go. Each one builds a piece of Milestone 7; beside each lesson is the piece it hands you.

- [Lesson 21 — AI as Programmer](https://davi-moreira.github.io/2026F_evidence_driven_research_purdue_HONR464/book/part4-credible-evidence/19-ai-as-programmer.html): your first computed number, its delegated code read line by line, and the sentence naming what the number does not cover.
- [Lesson 22 — AI as Analytical Assistant](https://davi-moreira.github.io/2026F_evidence_driven_research_purdue_HONR464/book/part4-credible-evidence/20-ai-as-analytical-assistant.html): your headline estimate with its cycle log, two independently re-derived numbers, and a placebo run.

When the last lesson closes, the milestone chapter is next. Nothing you write in a lesson is busywork: every piece above is on the milestone's checklist.
